title.title: QAOA attains the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick optimum
title.subtitle: Claim: with size to infinity first, finite-depth QAOA gets arbitrarily close to the SK ground-state energy

beats.text: Schematic: QAOA energy on the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model as depth grows
Size goes to infinity first, then depth; the angles do not depend on size
Claim: the energy reaches the true ground state, as the conjecture predicted

achievement.label: Conjecture of Basso–Farhi–Marwaha–Villalonga–Zhou (2022)
achievement.context: Before: energies computed at fixed depth; Montanari's classical algorithm assumes no overlap gap
achievement.note: No depth bound and no efficient way to choose the angles

verify.detail: Lean: Parisi-measure facts, conditional on a minimizer. Not QAOA convergence
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

sources.quote: No bound on the needed depth and no efficient angle selection

plain: A quantum optimization recipe, run deep enough, finds the best energy of a classic disordered magnet model

voice.text: Run the quantum approximate optimization algorithm on the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin glass.
Let size grow first and depth after, with fixed angles.
Claimed: it gets arbitrarily close to the true ground state.
